prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor hallway where the camera wearer's extended hands and a yellow-white jacket at ~0.3–0.6 m in the lower-left and centre of frame 1 are flanked by a near left wall (<0.3 m) and a darker region behind them (~1–2 m). Across frames 2 to 4, the jacket moves upward and closer to <0.3 m (bright grey-white) within immediate arm's reach as it passes over or right in front of the camera, heavily occluding the room and any person's head or torso, before clearing in frame 5 to reveal a left doorframe (<0.4 m), a small animal on the floor at bottom-centre (~1.0–1.5 m), a mid-ground corridor wall (~2–3 m), and a distant living room with a sofa (~5–7 m) to the upper right. Because the wearer and any nearby person are cropped below or behind the close fabric in frames 1–4 and absent from frame 5, no face orientation or gaze toward the camera wearer is visible. This map reveals smooth surface relief and relative distances of the dark foreground sleeves and shadowed hallway walls in frames 1–4 that are nearly pitch-black in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable where lighting changes and dark colours distort distance, such as rendering a shadowed patch in frame 1 and the brightly lit distant living room in frame 5 as pitch-black while over-smoothing boundaries between the close jacket and background.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects only isolated foreground regions across the five frames: the camera wearer's bare right forearm and hand at the bottom-centre of frame 1 (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach) labelled 'person', nothing in frame 2, the close yellow-white jacket (~0.1–0.3 m, filling frame 3) mislabelled 'banana', a broad 'person' mask covering the jacket and dark background across frame 4 (~0.2–1.5 m), and a small black 'cat' on the floor at bottom-centre of frame 5 (~1.0–1.5 m, just beyond arm's reach and ~0.5–1.0 m in front of the doorway wall). In frame 1 the segmented right arm is positioned to the right of the unsegmented left hand and below the jacket, while in frame 5 the cat is below and to the left of the unsegmented distant sofa (~5–7 m) and faces away toward the upper-right corridor, with no person's head or gaze toward the camera visible in any frame. Across the sequence, the masks reflect the garment rising to fully occlude the camera view in frames 3–4 before retreating out of view in frame 5 as the camera turns toward the open hallway. Compared to the dark RGB strip, the mask in frame 5 clearly isolates the silhouette of the dark cat against the shadowed carpet, and frame 1 cleanly separates the wearer's right arm from the dark background. However, the map is highly unreliable, completely missing all walls, doors, furniture, the left hand in frame 1, and all objects in frame 2, while misclassifying the close jacket as a 'banana' in frame 3 and merging the jacket with the dark background into an oversized 'person' mask in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, displaying only a small cluster of seven yellow body keypoints in the upper-left and upper-centre of frame 4 where the close jacket (~0.2–0.5 m, within arm's reach) occupies the foreground. It fails to detect the camera wearer's visible hands and forearms in frame 1 (~0.3–0.5 m) with zero magenta hand markers, provides no scene layout or background object positions, and shows no valid head or torso skeleton to indicate whether anyone faces or looks toward the camera wearer. The sole change across the five frames is the brief appearance of the fragmented yellow dots in frame 4 as the bright fabric moves across the upper field of view and occludes the room behind it. While those points roughly correspond to the raised shoulder and sleeve area of the garment in frame 4, the map provides almost no spatial information beyond what is already visible in RGB. Overall, the pose map is extremely unreliable due to severe close-range occlusion, cropping of bodies outside the frame, and low lighting, resulting in total missed detections in frame 1 and disconnected, uncalibrated keypoints on the moving fabric in frame 4.
